requirements.title: CSE elective eligibility
requirements.summary: CSE 100–194 may count if unused elsewhere; CSE 180, 180R and 191 are excluded. Graduate coursework needs a petition.

requirements.title: Topics-course limit
requirements.summary: CSE 190 and graduate analogue CSE 291 share a maximum of twelve units / three distinct topics.

requirements.title: P/NP and special studies
requirements.summary: At most twelve P/NP units: up to eight in CSE 198/199/199H, four in CSE 197, and two in CSE 109. Exceeding the special-studies limit requires faculty-reviewed petition.

requirements.title: Global Ties limit
requirements.summary: Up to eight ENG 100D/L units within the special-studies maximum; ENG 100D may count only once.

requirements.title: Letter grades
requirements.summary: All courses require letter grades except courses offered only P/NP.

requirements.title: Graduate degree reuse
requirements.summary: Graduate coursework counted in the undergraduate degree cannot also count in a graduate degree.

requirements.title: University degree minimums
requirements.summary: Complete at least 180 quarter units, including 60 upper-division units, an approved major, and the enrolled college’s requirements. These degree totals include the major; they are not added to its 124 units.

requirements.title: Senior residence
requirements.summary: Complete 35 of the final 45 units in residence in the degree-awarding UC college/school. Provost exceptions may cover approved UC visitors, Education Abroad, UCDC or UC Sacramento. UCSD Extension concurrent enrollment does not qualify. Roosevelt publishes a different 36/44 rule, retained separately.

requirements.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion
requirements.summary: Pass one approved four-unit course at C− or P or better; an articulated equivalent transfer course can qualify. Applies to lower-division entrants from Fall 2011 and upper-division entrants from Fall 2013. Approved finite course pool remains unreviewed.

requirements.title: American History and Institutions alternatives
requirements.summary: Qualify through C or better high-school US history (one unit, or half history plus half civics/government), an approved UCSD course at C−/P, AP US history/government at least 3, IB higher History of Americas at least 5, the page’s historical SAT II threshold 550, prior accepted California-college satisfaction, or acceptable college history/government at C or better. F-1/J-1 temporary residents may petition the college provost. Approved course pool remains unreviewed.

requirements.title: Entry writing placement and completion
requirements.summary: Complete placement before enrollment if entry writing is unsatisfied. College-writing placement satisfies the requirement. AWP 3 allows three consecutive quarters; AWP 4A allows three, then 4B follows immediately. Failure of the 4B portfolio leads to AWP 3, with at most three more consecutive quarters or five total. Earn C or better in AWP 3 or 4B before college writing. External UC entry-qualification alternatives remain to be inventoried.

requirements.title: Completion-time limits from Fall 2019
requirements.summary: First-year entrants have twelve quarters and transfers six. Beyond the limit, an approved college completion plan is required. Summer, approved part-time quarters, and quarters withdrawn from all courses do not count. Earlier-entry unit-limit rules are distinct.

requirements.title: Graduation application
requirements.summary: File the degree/diploma application with the college by its deadline; late filing needs special approval. Finish all coursework by the filed quarter’s end, otherwise submit a new application.

requirements.title: Double-major approvals and unique work
requirements.summary: Good-standing students need both departments and the college provost to approve. Each major needs at least ten unique upper-division courses (40 units); lower-division overlap is unrestricted. Two Engineering majors are not allowed, nor ordinarily two within one department. Additional major-specific prohibitions must also be checked.

requirements.title: Continuing-student protection
requirements.summary: Requirement changes should not substantially obstruct continuing students. Colleges/departments may deny this protection after an interruption longer than two years; no automatic mapping of the tentative 2026 AI plan onto earlier entrants.

requirements.title: 2026–27 direct-admit restriction
requirements.summary: The dated tentative department page admits only students directly placed in AI by Admissions in 2026–27. Internal switches and selective-major entry into AI are unavailable. AI students may leave for another CSE major but cannot switch back under this policy; review is planned in 2027, without a guarantee of changed eligibility.

requirements.title: Department grade and overlap policy
requirements.summary: The department requires C− or better and letter grading for major work except its specified P/NP-only exceptions (CSE 89, 91, 95, 109, 197, 198, 199). Each course serves only one core, AI elective, breadth or open-elective requirement. Graduate enrollment needs instructor and departmental TEA approval; similar undergraduate/graduate credit may require petition. Tentative-page course eligibility differences remain explicit.

requirements.title: Revelle College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: For first-year entrants: five-course humanities sequence; one fine arts; two social sciences; three mathematics including calculus; five sciences including biology, chemistry and physics; and fourth-quarter language proficiency or approved exam/native-language route. IGETC transfers retain mathematics, science and HUM 100; from Fall 2024 transfers need HUM 100, and transfers without UC reciprocity need four sciences. UC reciprocity exempts lower-division GE. Finite lists remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: John Muir College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete four approved three-course sequences: social science; mathematics or natural science; and two of fine arts, humanities and languages (48 units). At most three major courses overlap GE. Complete letter-graded MCWP 40 and 50 (8 units), without AP/IB substitution. IGETC or UC-reciprocity transfers may waive GE sequences; IGETC transfers still take MCWP 125 or request MCWP 50. Finite sequence lists remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Thurgood Marshall College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: First-year GE: three-course Dimensions of Culture at UCSD for letter grades; one nonperformance fine art; biology, chemistry and physics; two mathematics/statistics/logic courses in the stated allowable combinations; two approved humanities/cultural studies; and four courses outside the major, including two upper-division and at least one upper-division writing course. Optional four-unit public service may replace one breadth and meet writing. Transfers retain one approved upper-division writing and one noncontiguous upper-division breadth course, with additional needs determined from credit. Approved lists remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Earl Warren College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete letter-graded WCWP 10A–B and the two Ethics and Society choices PHIL/POLI 27 and 28; two approved formal-skills courses. BS Engineering students complete two three-course area studies outside the major, one humanities/fine arts and one social sciences, each with at least two upper-division courses. Interdisciplinary studies require college approval; a minor may substitute. AP/IB may supply at most four units per area study. Certified transfers take WCWP 100 plus one upper-division course outside the major; other transfers take WCWP 100 and area studies. AI-specific engineering area-study applicability and finite pools need confirmation.

requirements.title: Eleanor Roosevelt College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: First-year GE: five MMW courses; two natural sciences; two quantitative methods; language through fourth quarter or proficiency; one four-unit fine art; three courses in one geographic region including two upper-division; and qualifying upper-division written work graded C− or better. Transfer pathways use MMW 121/121R/122 with additional language/GE conditions based on certification; unmet first-year writing adds MMW 12/13. The college prints residence 36 of final 44 units, unlike university 35/45. Approved pools and full transfer conditions remain unresolved.

requirements.title: Sixth College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete CAT 1–3; one information-technology fluency; seven inquiry courses (two social sciences, two humanities, two natural sciences, one math/logic); one statistics; two art-making; four-unit upper-division experiential learning; and four-unit upper-division CAT 125 or 125R. Transfer agreements may meet some lower-division requirements; approved pools and exact transfer applicability remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Seventh College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete SYN 1/1R, SYN 2/2R and SYN 100; two approved courses each in arts, humanities, natural sciences/engineering, quantitative reasoning and social sciences; and one 2–4 unit high-impact experience. Alternatives/high-impact may overlap major, minor and university requirements. All transfers retain SYN 100 and high-impact; recommended SYN 150 can satisfy high-impact if letter graded. Approved pools and additional transfer needs remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Eighth College pathway (only if enrolled here)
requirements.summary: Complete CCE 1, 2, 3 and 120, plus two approved courses each in arts, humanities, natural sciences, quantitative methods/engineering and social sciences. Breadth may overlap major, minor and university requirements. Certified transfers retain CCE 110 and 120; others receive individual credit evaluation. CCE courses require letter grades. The catalog explicitly lists the climate-change requirement for Fall 2024 and later admits; its approved pool remains unreviewed.

requirements.title: UC entry-writing test alternatives
requirements.summary: Qualify through AP English Language/Literature, Seminar or Research at least 3; IB English LanguageA higher level at least 5 or standard level at least 6; ACT ELA at least 30 or combined English+Reading at least 63 from one sitting; or pre-March 2024 paper SAT reading/writing at least 680. Digital SAT and ACT English alone do not satisfy ELWR. Official test scores are due July 15; these placement uses do not imply admission-test use.

requirements.title: UC entry-writing pre-enrollment course alternative
requirements.summary: Before UC enrollment, earn C or better in a UC-transferable composition course worth 3 semester or 4 quarter units at an institution accredited by a former regional accreditor. Otherwise follow the campus placement/completion route; UCSD’s specific AWP timeline remains separately represented.

requirements.title: Climate requirement applicability
requirements.summary: Regulation 600H applies to first-year/lower-division entrants from Fall 2024. Transfers are exempt. Pass one approved one-quarter course at C− or P or better; no four-unit minimum is inferred from the DEI rule.

requirements.title: Distance-education unit ceiling
requirements.summary: Regulation 600B4, enacted June 3, 2025, prohibits 50 percent or more of UCSD-earned units from designated distance courses unless the major is approved as a distance-education program. No AI exemption is presumed.

requirements.title: Residence and approved external-program exceptions
requirements.summary: Minimum UC residence is three terms; a summer course of at least 2 units can count as half a term. Normally 35 of final 45 units must be resident. Students completing all requirements in an approved EAP/UCDC/UC Sacramento/NRS ecology program may use the preceding 45 units; faculty may alternatively permit 35 of final 90, including final 12, resident units. Roosevelt’s 36/44 catalog discrepancy remains visible.

requirements.title: Climate course credit and overlap
requirements.summary: AP/IB does not satisfy the climate requirement, including AP-derived ESYS 10 credit. Approved courses may overlap GE, DEI, major or minor requirements. First-time first-year entrants from Fall 2024 are covered; earlier matriculants and incoming transfers are exempt. Term offering lists are scheduling information, not the complete approved pool.
